title: eval-harness: add per-prompt regression CI hook and quality gating improvements
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context and motivation: Our per-prompt regression checks are currently coarse-grained and run as a post-merge job. This PR introduces a lightweight CI hook that runs targeted prompt-set regressions and quality gating during PR validation for changed prompts and affected model routes. The goal is to catch quality regressions earlier, reduce post-merge rollbacks, and provide clearer failure signals tied to prompt sets.

What this changes: 1) New GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/eval-per-prompt-ci.yml) that executes a delta of prompts changed in the PR and runs a sampled subset of gating evals; 2) A deterministic selector (scripts/eval/select_prompts.py) that maps changed prompt files to registered prompt-set IDs; 3) Quality-gate integration with existing eval-harness metrics (scripts/eval/quality_gate.py) so failures are surfaced as commit status checks; 4) Console annotation support to link failing prompts to dashboard and example differences; 5) Small refactor to the harness runner to support a --sample-rate flag for faster CI runs.

Checklist: - [x] Add workflow that runs on pull_request and pull_request_target for changed files - [x] Prompt-selector that avoids full-suite runs for large repos - [x] Fail fast on regressions exceeding thresholds - [x] Emit structured annotations and links to eval dashboards - [x] Tests for selector and quality-gate logic - [x] Documentation in docs/eval/ci.md

Notes on design: The selector uses a cached mapping of prompt file globs to prompt-set IDs to quickly compute the minimal evaluation set. The quality gate applies thresholds on chosen metrics (exact-match, semantic-similarity, hallucination-rate) and supports per-prompt overrides defined in eval/prompt-metadata/*.yaml. To avoid flaky CI we run a sampled subset by default (sample_rate=0.25) with deterministic seeding derived from the PR number and branch name. For high-risk model routes teams can opt-in to run the full suite using the workflow_dispatch job.

Risk and mitigations: The main risk is increased CI latency for PRs touching many prompts; mitigated by sampling and the mapping to limit stimulations. We added a timeout guard (10m) for the hook and clear fallback messaging recommending dedicated eval runs for larger changes.

Related/previous work: refs ENG-2345 (eval-metrics-integration), previous CI hooks in eval-harness (multiple PRs).

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Can we avoid using pull_request_target to prevent elevated token access? Suggest switching to pull_request where possible and re-running relying actions in a separate job with read-only tokens.
Aisha Patel: Good point. switched main check to pull_request and kept a gated pull_request_target for dashboard annotation only; added explicit read-only token usage and documented the flow.
Lena Cho: The default thresholds look reasonable but add a small note on how teams can configure per-prompt thresholds. Also let's ensure the sample seeding is deterministic across reruns.
Aisha Patel: Added per-prompt overrides and deterministic seed logic (PR id + branch name) in select_prompts.py. Tests added to cover seed stability.
Marcus Nguyen: CI time on a large change hit ~8m in my run — consider lowering sample_rate or increasing parallelism if we see this widely.
Aisha Patel: Lowered default sample_rate to 0.25 and added a configurable concurrency param; documented trade-offs in docs/eval/ci.md.
release_notes: Add per-prompt regression CI hook: runs sampled prompt-set evaluations on PRs, integrates quality gating into CI, and provides console annotations linking failing prompts to dashboards. Default sample rate 0.25; teams can opt-in to full-suite runs.
notes: This PR was merged after two approvals and a green CI run. Follow-up items: monitor CI latency for prompt-heavy repos and add opt-out labels for very large changes.
